# Storefire

> StoreFire gives a WooCommerce shop a lighter, faster storefront without throwing away the WooCommerce shop behind it. WooCommerce keeps handling products, orders, customers and payments; StoreFire serves the storefront your customers actually browse.

StoreFire is an open-source project. The marketing site is at [https://storefire.online](https://storefire.online). A live demo store runs at [https://shop.storefire.online](https://shop.storefire.online).

## What problem it solves

WooCommerce stores accumulate themes, plugins, page builders, scripts and styles over time — and all of it travels to the customer's browser on every page load. StoreFire separates the storefront from that baggage without requiring a rebuild of the shop.

## How it works (verified facts)

- Frontend: Nuxt 4 + Vue 3 + Tailwind CSS
- Commerce backend: WooCommerce REST API (Odoo JSON-RPC also supported)
- Cart & checkout: CoCart — session-based, no login required
- Caching: Nitro cache, Cloudflare KV in production
- Images: Nuxt Image — avif/webp, responsive
- Hosting: Cloudflare Pages
- Source: https://github.com/the-junglist/storefire

## Pricing model

- Self-hosted: £0 — open source, run it yourself.
- Managed hosting: no monthly fee. A small share of each sale, agreed up front. No sale, no fee.

## FAQ (short answers)

### What is StoreFire?
A lighter storefront that sits in front of an existing WooCommerce shop. Customers get a faster site to browse; WooCommerce keeps running the shop behind it.

### Does StoreFire replace WooCommerce?
No. WooCommerce keeps handling products, orders, customers and payments. Only the part shoppers see changes.

### Do I need to rebuild my shop?
No. Your WooCommerce setup stays exactly as it is. StoreFire connects to it.

### What happens to my products and orders?
Nothing. They stay in WooCommerce, right where they are.

### Is StoreFire for developers?
You can run it yourself if you're comfortable deploying a web app — it's open source. Or contact the team about managed hosting.

### Can I use it with my existing WooCommerce store?
Yes — that's what it's built for.
